Short name for this load - becomes its MQTT topic and API path (lower case letters, digits and underscores)

What kind of load this is - it decides which settings apply. Pool heat pump, sauna, hot water tank and buffer tank are heated stores that EOS Connect schedules and releases itself. External energy budget takes a "needs X Wh by then" push and schedules it. External load profile takes a ready-made profile and injects it as given, with no release signal - use it for space heating or air conditioning
Include this load in the forecast and control it
Entity/item for this load's power draw in watts
Remove this load's measured history from the household base load. Leave on unless its power sensor overlaps another one - turning it off makes the forecast count this appliance twice
Lower numbers are planned first and get the cheapest slots when several managed loads compete for the same shared power budget
Entity/item for the stored medium's temperature in degrees Celsius
Target temperature in degrees Celsius
Optional entity/item holding the target temperature, when it is set elsewhere - overrides the fixed value above
How far below target the medium must fall before heating starts, in kelvin - stops the appliance hunting around its setpoint
Entity/item for the surrounding air temperature. A pool uses the outdoor forecast when this is empty; an indoor tank falls back to a fixed value
Stored volume in cubic metres. For a sauna this is a water-equivalent that reproduces its heat-up time - the calibration corrects it over time
Surface losing heat, in square metres
Starting guess for the heat loss coefficient in W/(m2 K). It is measured from the observed cooling rate and refined automatically
Electrical power the appliance draws while running, in watts
Coefficient of performance at 26 C ambient. Use 1.0 for a resistive heater such as a sauna. Refined automatically from measured operation
How much the COP changes per kelvin of ambient temperature, as a fraction of the nominal value. Refined automatically
Optional entity/item that is on when the cover is closed
Fraction of the heat loss that remains while the cover is closed

How the cheapest slots are chosen. Combined uses the grid price but values PV surplus at the feed-in tariff, so your own solar wins over cheap grid energy - recommended. Cheapest slots looks at the grid price only. PV surplus takes the sunniest slots first and falls back to price when there is no surplus
Shortest time the appliance stays released once started - protects the compressor from being cycled every time the plan is recalculated
Cap on released hours per day (0 = no cap)
First hour of the day the appliance may run (leave equal to end for no limit)
Hour of the day after which the appliance may no longer run
Hours from now by which the target must be reached (0 = anywhere in the next two days). A sauna wanted this evening sets it; a pool does not
Never run above this price in ct/kWh (0 = no cap). Ignored when frost protection is active
Never run below this ambient temperature - an air source heat pump barely works in the cold and its heat exchanger can freeze
Run immediately regardless of price when the medium falls to this temperature
First day of the season, as MM-DD (leave empty for all year)
Last day of the season, as MM-DD
How long pushed data stays valid. After this the load stops being counted, so a sender that goes quiet cannot hold a stale forecast forever
